segments.text: Good morning council. Barbara Tripp, Tampa Fire Rescue fire chief. Today, it is my honor to introduce Captain James Mcgregor as our firefighter of the quarter. Captain Mcgregor served at Tampa Fire Rescue over 19 years. Throughout his career with Tampa Fire Rescue he has consistently demonstrated commitment to excellence, professionalism and service, whether he is leading his crew, mentoring new firefighters, teaching in the classroom or serving as active district chief, he approaches every responsibility with the same level of dedication and purpose. He is constantly seeking opportunity to learn, to improve, and to bring knowledge back to his crew as well as Tampa Fire Rescue. Through additional education, training certificates and attending training programs across the country, he has developed an impressive depth of knowledge. More importantly, willing to share the knowledge with others, helping develop the next generation of firefighters through recruit training, in-service instructions and day-to-day mentorship. He's commit -- his commitment to service extends beyond the fire service. Before joining Tampa Fire Rescue, Captain Mcgregor served our nation with distinct and pride in the United States Marine Corps for 20 years. This includes seven years active duty and 13 years of reserve. He was assigned to the Hmx One, presidential helicopter squadron. Actually oversaw that. Serving as helicopter crew, where he earned the presidential service badge. In addition, he served multiple deployments during his military career as a foreign security advisor in support of oif, oef, two major post-9/11 u.s. Combat operations. The discipline, leadership, and selfless service that define his military career continues to be evident in everything he does today. One of his greatest strengths is his dependability where challenge is he tackle and project to complete a problem. Captain Mcgregor is always willing to assist. He leads by examples, earns the respect of those he works alongside and consistently demonstrate the values that define professional. Captain Mcgregor dedication to personal and professional development and genuine desire to make those around him better have a tremendous impact on Tampa Fire Rescue. His passion for service in our country and our community makes him deserving of this award. Please join me in congratulating Captain Mcgregor as firefighter of the quarter. [ applause ]

segments.text: Thank you. Item number 53. And then we'll hear from Barbara Tripp after this. Patrick Messmer, Tampa Police Department. We are here basically to make some minor amendments to the school zone speed camera enforcement ordinance that council has already passed. We already passed the contract, the ordinance. We have one simple goal and that's to protect students and to protect our folks who are walking to school, who are driving to school, and what we have done, I think council is pretty much familiar with this program. It was previously passed. We relied on a study from the Hillsborough County Transportation Planning Commission that was commissioned back in 2022. It actually used some data as old as 2018 and it relied on a lot of multimodal aspects of walking and biking to school, things like that. When we had some issues with the previous vendor, some operational issues and we were basically severed the ties with the previous vendor, when we adopted the new contract and moved to red speed, red speed offered to actually do a true speed study. So we had them do the speed study at 31 school zones in the City Of Tampa. And they specifically were looking for the number of speeding vehicles that would be committing a violation under this statute during school hours. So we identified 18 specific school zones. These schools were actually a little bit more geographically spread out through the city than the original study showed. But there are 18 of the school zones that average between 200 and even up to 3,000 speeding violations per day. What we're asking council to do is to amend the ordinance and again the only amendment is to just change the locations. 6 of the previous locations that were already in the ordinance were also identified in this study, but there were some additional locations that had a lot of these serious speeding issues that were identified. So because our goal is making our school zones safer, making our students safer as they are coming to school, we do want to make sure that the locations that have the most speeding violations are the ones that were actually putting our speed cameras at. I know there's been some concern about the potential for sharing of any kind of data, license plate readers and so forth. Just a reminder, both the state statute and city ordinance do not allow the sharing of any kind of data for surveillance purposes. There will be none of that. Even if the state statute gets amended and allows that, the city ordinance will prohibits the use of this kind of data for surveillance purposes. There can be no data sharing with any kind of a license plate recognition system that can be used for surveillance in the future. If the vendor were to do that, they would be in breach of the city ordinance and breach of the contract. We don't have any concern. That's not going to happen. We've spoken with them. They are not going to be storing this data for any kind of license plate recognition purposes, any kind of surveillance purposes. As a reminder, these violations do not carry any points on a person's driver's license, even if the violation turns into a uniform traffic citation, it's not paid, it still does not generate points on somebody's driver's license. We do know that these cameras make school zones safer, depending on what study you look at, anywhere from 45% to an 80% reduction in speeding from when these cameras are installed. So we definitely know that they are valuable. They are a valuable public safety piece. Of course, before this is implemented, we do hope that it is implemented here by the start of the school year. We do plan to have a robust public education campaign. We're going to be -- this is an item. Some of the data is old because it is from the old system. Can you all see that? That's just an example of one of the flyers that we post either on social media or we give out at community meetings. So some of those dates on there are obviously going to change. But we also have -- these are just a couple of screen shots from the previous website that we set up again on this. The website has been archived right now because it's not active, but we do have a website set up. We have videos. We have a lot of examples. We have frequently asked questions. We have location data that will be on these websites. Again, we plan on not only are we going to promote the website, not only promote things via social media, we plan on going to community meetings to get with community groups, make sure that we notify them that the program is going to be starting. There is a 30 day warning period when each camera is set up before violations start being issued. So the warning period and the robust community outreach is very important to us. Again, we're asking for council to just approve this amendment so we can put these cameras at our most important locations where speeding has been determined via the traffic study to be an issue. We would ask council support on this. I'm here to answer any questions along with Mr. Schmid and Mr. Riser.

Under Florida contract law, a binding contract requires three elements -- offer, acceptance, and consideration. Along with a meeting of the minds between the parties. The requirement of two distinct parties is implicit. The City Of Tampa is a single municipal corporation, i.e. Single party. And a legal entity under chapter 166 Florida statutes. City departments are divisions of the city and do not possess a separate legal existence. Because the departments are not separate legal entities, an agreement between two City departments is legally equivalent to the city entering into an agreement with itself. Florida courts have held that municipal departments lack a separate legal existence from the municipality itself. So therefore even if an interdepartmental agreement were approved by City Council and signed by the mayor, the fundamental problem still remains. There are not two separate legal parties to the agreement and City Council approval cannot create a second contract party where none exists. Any interdepartmental agreement has no legal effect. segments.text: My last and more pleasant motion is -- this will be good for Councilman Viera since they are performing up there -- I would like to make a motion for the Tampa City Ballet to provide a presentation on September 17, 2026, about their -- the impact that they are making on the community and the mission of making professional dance accessible throughout Tampa Bay.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: Motion from the chair. I have a second from Councilman Maniscalco. I have to say, they e-mailed me and asked me to come and see a show. I went to see the new ballet works which was unbelievable innovative. It was so incredibly cool. Went to see the video game one. It was absolutely amazing. Just one of the best live performances i've seen in a really long time. I highly recommend if you have not had the chance to go to the Tampa Ballet that you do so. I have a motion and a second.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: Let me say something, too. This fall when they come back, they are on break for summer. They have la septima. If you haven't seen that, that is Tampa Bay's cigar -- amazing. Absolutely incredible.

segments.speaker: Bill Carlson
segments.text: Is the one you're talking about still there?

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: They are out for break.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: It was only for three days. It was unbelievable. So fast. Obviously, we want to do more for the ballet, but really, I would love for them -- we could barely -- we went to the very first performance which was a matinee on a Saturday. They had Saturday night and Sunday and that was it. We just wanted to tell the world about it. But unfortunately we just didn't have time. Any Way that we could find to extend their runs so that more people could see. It was the most innovative, interesting thing. They had like a Graphic Designer from Apple who had created this projection on the back wall, on the floor and on the whole sides of the theater. And they were acting like they were in a video game. So they were hopping and jumping. It kind of did go back to super mario brothers where they would hit something and something would -- they did a running game. Similar to the car racing games. It was truly amazing. That was only one of the amazing performances.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: I took my Five-Year-Old Granddaughter up. Again, plug for New Tampa.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: Beautiful space.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: Really nice space. And we Did That Drive to Tampa. My Five-Year-Old Granddaughter and she just started at the straz this last week, summer ballet program. Inspired. We went to see sleeping beauty.

segments.speaker: Luis Viera
segments.text: You are five minutes away from where I live, hunter's green right in front of it. That passed. In the county commission it almost failed. Victor Crist's baby and Ken Hagan took it over and almost failed. City intervened and promised to do maintenance on it. It's a great thing.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: Great asset for the community.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: We have to vote on this. I have a motion from Chair Clendenin and who seconded it? Council member Maniscalco. All in favor? Aye. I do have one more thing I did want to mention because Councilwoman Young mentioned the land development code updates. They have been great. We had one in South Tampa on Monday. That was very well attended. We had a great one in East Tampa on Tuesday, also well attended, North Tampa was last night. Had some really good conversations. I highly recommend anybody who hasn't been able to make it out come to Barksdale Community Center at 6:30 on Monday night, June 8.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: You all be nice to staff.

segments.speaker: Lynn Hurtak
segments.text: They were. People are very passionate about it, but some really great ideas have come from all of it. I really enjoyed the time.

segments.speaker: Bill Carlson
segments.text: Make a motion to ask staff to fix the squeaky door?

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: I like the squeaky door. I can tell when people are coming in.

segments.speaker: Luis Viera
segments.text: Time me for one minute. It's on Rory Jones that all of us know who is obviously with our Water Department. He came out to a meeting at Forest Hills to talk about some drought issues. It was pouring rain out there. He went out there. I know, right? It was pouring rain out there and he did a great job. He was very patient. I want to say this publicly. He ran into somebody there who was extremely rude to him. And it just pissed me off because he is a nice guy. I told the mayor and chief Bennett about it, but I just wanted to publicly salute rory for having patience and resiliency in the face of a little something. That's all. He's a good guy.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: It's a reminder that we're elected and getting yelled at and stuff. The staff, they are employees and they are working here. A lot of them are working many, many hours. I think -- I ask the public to give them the deference for that. I have a motion to receive and file from Councilman Maniscalco. Second from Councilman Miranda. All those in favor, aye. Opposed? Ayes have it. We are adjourned.
